chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sharif ibn Sabiq, from Al-Fadl ibn Abi Qurra, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
'There is no believer except that he has humor (playfulness); I said, 'And what is the humor?' He said, 'Al-mizah (joyful banter/teasing).'

key_terms.الْمِزَاحُ: Joyful banter, teasing, or playful conversation

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic definition of humor in a believer according to Hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that 'al-mizah' (lighthearted banter) is an inherent trait of every believer, countering the notion that piety requires perpetual solemnity. This narration is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for defining the boundaries of permissible humor, emphasizing that joy and playfulness are spiritual virtues when practiced with moderation and sincerity.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Shareef Bin Sabiq, from Al Fazl Bin Abu Qurra, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘There is none from a Momin except there is humour in him’. I said, ‘And what is the humour?’ Heasws said: ‘The (tales in) joyful (manners)’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Sharif ibn Sabiq from al-Fadl ibn abu Qarrah from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Every believing person knows how to tell funny stories. I asked, ‘What is cd-Dci’cibahT The Imam said, ‘It is funny stories.’”
